title: Microsoft Releases .NET 11 RC1 with Go-Live Support, C# 15 and F# 11 as Default Language Versions
gist: Microsoft shipped .NET 11 RC1 under a go-live production license, promoting C# 15 and F# 11 to default language versions and stabilizing union types, closed class hierarchies and collection expression arguments. Adoption friction reported by developers is unusually low — an SDK install plus project-file edits — but union types do not round-trip through System.Text.Json because the serialized output carries no type discriminator.

themes.theme: Go-live licensing pulls production adoption forward

insights.claim: Microsoft's .NET 11 Release Candidate 1 ships with a go-live support license, allowing teams to run it in production applications before general availability.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Go-live licensing compresses the usual enterprise wait between RC and GA, pulling platform-migration revenue and tooling demand forward a quarter.
insights.locator: Last week, Microsoft has released .NET 11 Release Candidate 1

insights.claim: Developers reported that moving an existing codebase to the new .NET release took little more than an SDK install and a few project-file edits, and at least one said the go-live license alone was enough to move containers into production.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Near-zero migration cost is the strongest predictor of fast .NET version uptake — contrast with the multi-year lag on Java LTS migrations.
insights.locator: Community reaction in the Reddit discussion was mostly practical.

insights.claim: At least one developer left the long-term support track specifically to get closed class hierarchies, meaning individual language features are now strong enough to override support-lifecycle policy.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Feature pull beating LTS discipline signals the language is genuinely differentiating, and fragments the support-version mix enterprises must maintain.
insights.locator: Another said closed class hierarchies were the reason

insights.claim: RC1 is supported only in the new Visual Studio 2026 Insiders release and in Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Early adoption requires riding an Insiders IDE channel, which gates how much of the enterprise base can actually take the go-live offer.
insights.locator: .NET 11 RC1 is supported in the new Visual Studio 2026 Insiders

themes.theme: C# 15 stabilizes and union types ship

insights.claim: C# 15 becomes the default language version for projects targeting .NET 11 and stabilizes collection expression arguments, union types, non-virtual static interface members, closed class hierarchies, labeled break and continue, and extension indexers.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Default-version promotion means these features reach the whole installed base by default, not just opt-in early adopters.
insights.locator: Release Candidate 1 makes C# 15 the default language version

insights.claim: Union types no longer require the preview language setting, Roslyn now uses the final CSharp15 names, and a new API exposes a union's cases to analyzers.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Analyzer-visible union cases create a new surface for static-analysis and code-quality tool vendors to build on.
insights.locator: Union types no longer require the preview language setting.

insights.claim: The main community criticism of the release is that C# union types do not round-trip through System.Text.Json because the serialized output carries no type discriminator.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: A flagship language feature that breaks the default serializer limits its use in APIs and persistence layers — expect workarounds and third-party converters before real adoption.
insights.locator: The main criticism concerned union types

insights.claim: Unsafe Evolution remains a preview feature behind its own flag, though RC1 now allows await inside an unsafe context.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Signals which C# capabilities are still a release cycle or more away from production-safe use.
insights.locator: Unsafe Evolution stays a preview feature with its own flag

insights.claim: Microsoft's Jon Galloway clarified that .NET release posts list changes since the previous preview rather than since the prior major version, meaning readers systematically underestimate the cumulative delta.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Incremental release notes understate the true upgrade surface — do not size a .NET migration from a single release post.
insights.locator: Jon Galloway, from Microsoft's .NET team, replied in the thread

themes.theme: F# 11 drops reflection for AOT compatibility

insights.claim: F# 11 string interpolation now compiles to String.Concat instead of the reflection-based printf engine, which makes it work with trimming and Native AOT.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Removing reflection unblocks F# for trimmed, ahead-of-time-compiled deployments — the serverless and container cold-start use case.
insights.locator: string interpolation now compiles to String.Concat

insights.claim: F# 11 becomes the default language version and adds reflection-free ToString output for records and unions, record spreads, direct delegate construction, inheritdoc and include documentation tags, and Async.RunSynchronouslyImmediate.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: The consistent theme is eliminating reflection dependencies — the prerequisite for F# in AOT-constrained cloud runtimes.
insights.locator: F# 11 is also the default language version.

insights.claim: The .NET SDK's dotnet test can now run test projects targeting Android, iOS, macOS and Mac Catalyst with new project templates for each, plus run-level options for timeouts, stopping after N failures, and per-application results directories.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: First-party mobile test tooling reduces reliance on third-party mobile CI vendors in the .NET ecosystem.
insights.locator: In the SDK, dotnet test can now run test projects

insights.claim: Container publishing can now produce the same image digest across builds when SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is set, and it skips uploads when the image manifest already exists in the target registry.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Reproducible digests are the building block for supply-chain attestation and cut registry bandwidth/storage spend on repeat builds.
insights.locator: container publishing can produce the same image digest

themes.theme: Web, identity and mobile surface changes

insights.claim: ASP.NET Core finalizes SignalR authentication refresh APIs across server, .NET client and TypeScript client, and Blazor Server circuits now pick up a refreshed identity without reconnecting.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Removing the reconnect on token refresh eliminates a visible failure mode in long-lived real-time apps — a quiet reliability win for Blazor-based products.
insights.locator: ASP.NET Core finalizes the SignalR authentication refresh APIs

insights.claim: The package for Device Bound Session Credentials remains experimental and will stay prerelease throughout the entire .NET 11 cycle.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Token-binding-based session security is pushed out at least one full major version — relevant to anyone timing DBSC-dependent security roadmaps.
insights.locator: the package for Device Bound Session Credentials remains experimental

insights.claim: .NET MAUI extends dotnet test to mobile and desktop targets and adds TabbedPage badges, explicit SwipeItem colors, themed splash screens and faster, smaller Android builds.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Continued MAUI investment keeps Microsoft's cross-platform mobile story alive against Flutter and React Native, though the changes are incremental polish.
insights.locator: .NET MAUI extends dotnet test to mobile and desktop targets

insights.claim: OpenAPI documents now mark obsolete operations, types and properties as deprecated, and validation localization moves from a preview API to resource-name conventions.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Machine-readable deprecation in generated specs makes automated client-side migration and API-lifecycle tooling viable.
